reason: The handler accepts an arbitrary URL, navigates a browser tab to it, and includes a snapshot in the response. That supports UNTRUSTED because attacker-controlled web content from a supplied URL can be returned, and SINK because navigating to an agent-supplied URL sends a request/data to an agent-chosen host. The README line states file:// navigation is normally blocked but can be allowed with an unrestricted file-access option; combined with the included snapshot, these lines support that file:// content it can reach may be returned, so SECRET is supported. Nothing in the cited lines shows arbitrary host code execution; browser page execution is not HOSTEXEC.
